analysis.title: Rates Spark: US and France like ships passing in the night at 5%
key_insights: The US 10yr Treasury yield broke back below 5% around midday in New York on Thursday with conviction. ING expects it to ultimately revert back above 5%, citing inflation, fiscal deficit and AI boom underpinnings, though timing is uncertain.

Buyers have stepped into 5%+ levels for the US 10yr in recent weeks. After the recent poor CPI number, Treasuries sold off immediately and then rallied by more, and the break below 5% is the culmination of that move.
The risk-off environment takes pressure off the Fed to hike next week. ING still would not load up on duration at current levels.
Neither side has a plan for the US fiscal deficit as the mid-term elections approach in the next couple of weeks, which ING flags as a source of trouble for yields.
French 10yr yields are above 5% and the spread over Bunds reached 177bp, versus a late-2011 peak just under 200bp. ING expects a new high within days and sees no catalyst to stop the widening.

The latest French spread widening is driven by deteriorating general sentiment rather than French headlines. Uncertainty until the presidential elections keeps investors sidelined, and French bonds cannot benefit from a sentiment recovery.

Moody's reviews France after markets close on Friday. It is at Aa3 with a negative outlook, one notch above the other two major agencies (A+, stable outlooks). ING calls a downgrade overdue and a catch-up, and expects commentary to be parsed for further downgrade triggers.
Moody's has no fixed release time. Its 2024 France downgrade hit the wires just after midnight CET.
Lasting relief for French bonds needs positive news such as a 2027 budget with some fiscal consolidation, which may have to wait until December.
Brent oil rose above $110 for the first time since May, but weaker market sentiment prevented a hawkish repricing in rates.

Friday's PMIs are the next test. Weak data would risk a bullish repricing in rates, and for euro rates a weaker growth outlook combined with French turmoil would push markets to turn more dovish on the ECB.
Thursday was the first day of pronounced flight into Bunds since the French problems began, and Treasuries shared in the move.

tension_points.bull_case: Risk-off flows and buying into 5%+ levels pushed the yield below 5%, and the risk-off tone takes pressure off the Fed to hike next week. Weak PMIs could trigger a bullish repricing in rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation, fiscal deficit and AI boom underpinnings, plus the mid-term elections with no deficit plan, argue for the yield snapping back above 5%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Calm returning to risk markets would allow the 10yr yield to move back above 5%.
